reason: Base UI draws Checkbox and Radio as a span, so shadcn's disabled:opacity-50 (a :disabled selector) never matches and a disabled control stays fully opaque upstream; maia reads [data-disabled] instead, which is what the utility means. An upstream defect, not a maia value. Same as foundation's.

The preset is generated with rtl:false, so its paddings and radii are physical (pl-/pr-, rounded-l-) and do not mirror under dir=rtl; the layer-3 rules are logical. The section proves DirectionProvider renders, not a value. Same as foundation's.

A preset app's globals.css carries no .cn-* rules, so the cn-input-otp class the shadcn component keeps is unstyled there; style-maia.css's `.cn-input-otp { gap-2 }` is maia's own value and the system keeps it. Same as foundation's.

The shortcuts contain ⌘, which is in neither Figtree build: the reference app falls back through next/font's Figtree Fallback and the preview through Figtree Variable plus the Pretendard Hangul fallback, so the glyph advance differs by 0.5–1px. Font stack, not a value.

Dark mode only: Tailwind sorts maia's dark:aria-invalid:border-destructive/50 after aria-invalid:aria-checked:border-primary, which has no dark counterpart, so upstream an invalid checked checkbox loses its checked border in dark. maia keeps the state colour; reproducing the ordering would delete the signal. Same shape as foundation's dark-ordering row, narrowed to the one element maia shows it on.
